# Agentic ODI [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **[![Experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/Experimental-1e293b?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi)** > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- **Agentic ODI** explores how the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server acts as the "brain" of customer needs — letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in verified, measurable customer outcomes (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores). This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) of six installable Python projects plus the React `studio/` front end, each with its own build, tests, and layout: | Package | Description | |---|---| | **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`) | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, and repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), including ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`) | A foundational MCP Server exposing an HTTP transport layer. It hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value). | | **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`) | The FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. It talks to the MCP server on the client's behalf and serves the Studio API — configuration, health probes, canvas data, MCP mutations, and streaming (SSE) chat with the LLM tool-loop — plus the built SPA when `studio/dist` exists. | | **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`) | The local dev **launcher** (`run.py` / `python -m client.run`) that starts the MCP server and the Studio sidecar together. | | **`apps/studio/`** (React + TypeScript + Vite) | **The Living Studio** front end — a spatial, conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation with an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous copilot. The copilot renders **agent-composed cards inline** (scored outcomes, opportunity boards, bet simulations) from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A skippable four-step **first-run tour** (feature-flagged, in `apps/studio/src/onboarding/`) ends in a real first prompt. Ships as a browser SPA and as a **Tauri 2 desktop app** (`apps/studio/src-tauri/`). | | **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`) | A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface with an interactive chat mode plus `version`, `update`, `connectors`, and `customer-outcomes` (alias `outcomes`) commands. Data commands are local-first (`--backend local`, default) or remote (`--backend mcp`), with readable tables, `--json`, and a top-level `score`. | | **`connectors/`** (`agentic-odi-connectors`) | Pluggable external integrations. The first kind is an **MCP client connector** that connects to a remote MCP server over HTTP, checks health, and ingests tools/resources into a local ingest sink. Additional kinds (REST, webhooks, and so on) can register against the same protocol later. | ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager. ```bash # Install the entire workspace (all six projects plus dev tooling) uv sync --all-packages # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together npm --prefix studio run build python -m client.run ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | For hot reload, `npm --prefix studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support to drive its agent — see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md). ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m cli --help # show available options and commands python -m cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m mcp_server`). See the [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md). ### Install the binary Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` The installer symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`. See [Installation](docs/installation.md) for the install layout, updates, and release automation. ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | |---|---| | [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md) | Backends, interactive chat, `customer-outcomes`, `connectors`, scoring, environment variables | | [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md) | The MCP ingest connector, presets, and the `Connector` protocol | | [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md) | Run modes, the first-run wizard and its feature flag, rich inline responses and the UI catalog, desktop signing and updates, agent-driven testing (`/dev`, `/test`) | | [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md) | Running a local OpenAI-compatible model with tool calling | | [Development](docs/development.md) | Lint, format, type checks, frontend checks, tests and the coverage map | | [Installation](docs/installation.md) | Binary install, updater behavior, and release automation | | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) | Hosted chat UI and the MCP server endpoint | | [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) | Completed and upcoming milestones | | [Superpowers](docs/superpowers.md) | Pi, OpenCode, and Freebuff integration | ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! This project uses [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) for linting and formatting and [pytest](https://pytest.org/) for tests. Make sure your change passes the [lint, format, and test checks](docs/development.md) before opening a pull request. ## License No license has been specified for this repository yet. Until one is added, all rights reserved by the maintainers. Please reach out before reuse or redistribution. ---
*Let's build AI that builds what people actually need.*

display.text:
# Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend

To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a
local LLM backend that:

- Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example,
  `/v1/chat/completions`), and
- Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**.

A simple fully local option is
[`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run
a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server.

## 1. Install a local LLM server

Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for
platform-specific build notes):

```bash
pip install llama-cpp-python
```

## 2. Download a small tools-capable model

Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a
7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g.
`C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`.

## 3. Start the OpenAI-compatible server

Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default
used by the Living Studio sidecar and the CLI chat:

```bash
python -m llama_cpp.server \
  --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \
  --model_alias local-tools-model \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \
  --chat_format openai
```

This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`.

## 4. Configure the Studio

The Living Studio sidecar and the CLI chat read the following environment
variables (with sensible defaults):

| Variable | Default |
|---|---|
| `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` |

You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Living Studio's
**Settings** panel.

## 5. Verify tool-calling against the MCP server

- (Optional) Before starting the UI, confirm the LLM backend is reachable:

  ```bash
  curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models
  ```

  If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before
  debugging the MCP client/server.

- Start the MCP server and Studio (via `python -m client.run` or one of the
  [run modes](living-studio.md)).
- In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for
  example: *"Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI
  repository."*
- You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for
  example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI
  guidance, confirming the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work
  together.
- If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI shows a clear error
  banner indicating the configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with
  details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps
  above to fix your local LLM setup.

parts.text:
Now I have a good understanding. Let me think about the design.

The request: "add mic capabilities so that the user may speak to chat".

Key decisions to make:
1. Where does the mic live? The Studio SPA (browser + Tauri) is the primary chat UI. The CLI is a terminal REPL. The most natural place is the Studio SPA.
2. How does transcription happen? Options:
   - **Browser-native `SpeechRecognition`** (Web Speech API): Chrome/Edge only, no network needed from our side, but doesn't work in Tauri webview (WebKitGTK) reliably, and doesn't work in Firefox/Safari.
   - **Record audio (MediaRecorder) → POST to sidecar → ASR**: works everywhere the browser supports MediaRecorder (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari 14.1+), and works in Tauri webview. Needs a transcription backend.
   - **Backend transcription**: sidecar endpoint that forwards to an OpenAI-compatible Whisper endpoint, or a local whisper. The project is local-first with OpenAI-compatible endpoints. The `base_url` setting points to an OpenAI-compatible server. OpenAI's API has `/v1/audio/transcriptions` (Whisper). llama.cpp server also supports `/v1/audio/transcriptions`? Actually llama-cpp-python has an audio transcription endpoint at `/v1/audio/transcriptions` in some versions. Hmm.

Let me think about what fits this project best. The project is local-first, and the sidecar already proxies to the OpenAI-compatible backend. The cleanest approach: sidecar gets a `POST /api/transcribe` endpoint that takes multipart audio, and calls the OpenAI-compatible `/audio/transcriptions` endpoint using the configured `base_url` + `api_key`. This works with OpenAI, and with any OpenAI-compatible server that implements Whisper (llama.cpp, LocalAI, vLLM's whisper variant, LM Studio, etc.).

But there's a risk: local LLM servers (llama-cpp with a text model) won't have an audio transcription endpoint. So we need graceful degradation.

Alternative: browser `SpeechRecognition` (Web Speech API) does the transcription in-browser using the browser's own cloud service (Chrome sends audio to Google). That's a privacy concern for a local-first project, and doesn't work in the Tauri webview (WebKitGTK has no SpeechRecognition).

Let me consider: what's the most robust, self-contained approach that works in the Tauri desktop app?

Option A: MediaRecorder → sidecar → OpenAI-compatible `/audio/transcriptions`.
- Works in browser + Tauri (WebKitGTK supports MediaRecorder? WebKitGTK's MediaRecorder support... Safari supports MediaRecorder since 14.1. WebKitGTK is a port of Safari's WebKit, so it should support MediaRecorder with audio. Tauri on Linux uses WebKitGTK. Support is plausible but not guaranteed.)
- Requires network/LLM endpoint with audio support.
- Clean, testable backend.

Option B: Browser SpeechRecognition only.
- Simplest, zero backend. But Chrome-only, sends to Google.

Option C: Both — a layered approach with a preference order.

Given the project architecture (SPA ↔ sidecar ↔ LLM), Option A is the architecturally consistent choice. The SPA never talks to the LLM directly — it always goes through the sidecar. So transcription should also go through the sidecar. That's a strong architectural argument.

But we should consider: should the transcription be a separate model setting, or reuse the LLM base_url? The OpenAI audio transcription endpoint is `<base_url>/audio/transcriptions`. For a local llama.cpp server, that may 404. So we need a separate configurable "transcription endpoint" or reuse base_url with graceful error.

Let me think about the fallback design. I think a good design:

- New settings field: `stt_url` (or `transcription_url`) — optional. If empty, derive from `base_url` by replacing `/v1` with `/v1` and appending `/audio/transcriptions`? Hmm, simpler: `transcription_base_url` optional; default = `base_url` (so `<base_url>/audio/transcriptions`).
- Sidecar: `POST /api/transcribe` (multipart file upload) → returns `{"text": "..."}`.
- Sidecar: `POST /api/health/stt` maybe. Or fold into the config.

Actually, let me reconsider. A cleaner approach given the "settings" object: add `transcription_url` to StudioConfig, defaulting to empty which means "derive from base_url". The SettingsPanel gets a field.

3. **Use the existing LLM backend's OpenAI-compatible audio endpoint** — the base_url is already configured. If the user points at a local LLM (llama.cpp), audio transcription isn't supported.

The most consistent with the project's philosophy ("the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM directly", everything goes through the sidecar which holds the API key) is: capture in the browser, transcribe server-side in the sidecar, then the resulting text goes into the draft/send path.

ChannelSection titled “Channel”
Source: https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/core.ts#L119
A message channel used to stream values from Rust to the frontend.

Key finding: Tauri's JS API has no `getUserMedia` permission. `getUserMedia` in a Tauri webview is subject to webview's own permission handling. On Linux WebKitGTK, `getUserMedia` is typically NOT supported. On macOS WKWebView, `getUserMedia` works but requires `NSCameraUsageDescription`/`NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` in Info.plist, and Tauri v2 supports `bundle.macOS.entitlements` / `Info.plist` via `bundle.macOS.infoPlist`? Let me check that quickly.

Actually, there's a much more important architectural decision here. Let me think about the design space:

**Where does transcription happen?**
1. **Browser Web Speech API (`SpeechRecognition`)** — Chrome/Edge only, no Tauri WebKit support, no server, free. But poor support, sends audio to Google servers.
2. **Server-side STT via OpenAI-compatible Whisper endpoint** — the sidecar already talks to an OpenAI-compatible base_url. Many local setups (faster-whisper-server, whisper.cpp server, LocalAI, Ollama) expose `/v1/audio/transcriptions`. The `openai` Python SDK has `client.audio.transcriptions.create()`. This works in browser AND Tauri (audio captured via MediaRecorder → uploaded to sidecar → transcribed).

**Where is audio captured?**
1. **Browser MediaRecorder + getUserMedia** — works in the browser SPA; in Tauri (WebKitGTK) getUserMedia is generally not supported on Linux. WKWebView on macOS supports it with Info.plist usage descriptions.
2. **Tauri native capture** — new Rust plugin, heavy.

**How to get audio from browser to server?** Options:
- Multipart POST to a new sidecar endpoint `/api/transcribe`. Needs `python-multipart` (already installed transitively but not declared in studio-api pyproject — need to add).
- Or base64 JSON POST (no new dependency). Simpler; audio is small (webm/opus).

Let me now consider the alternative: **Web Speech API only** — zero backend, zero deps, but Tauri doesn't support it (webkit doesn't implement SpeechRecognition).

Given the repo ships a Tauri desktop app AND a browser SPA, and the design goal is "the user may speak to chat", I think the right architecture is:

- **Capture**: MediaRecorder in the SPA (works in browser). For Tauri, we need to check if getUserMedia works. On Linux WebKitGTK, `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia` is not implemented → mic simply unavailable in the Linux desktop app. macOS WKWebView: it does support getUserMedia since macOS 10.14 but requires Info.plist `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`. Tauri v2 config supports `bundle.macOS.infoPlist`? Let me check the desktop-schema.

Let me check the Tauri v2 config schema for macOS Info.plist / entitlements.

Actually, let me be efficient. The critical unknowns I should confirm:
1. Tauri v2 bundle config: can we set `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` in Info.plist? → `bundle.macOS.infoPlist`? Hmm. Actually in Tauri v2 I don't think there's an `infoPlist` key; there's `bundle.macOS.entitlements` and `bundle.macOS.entitlements` only. Actually, Tauri v2 does NOT have an infoPlist config option. Tauri v1 had `tauri.bundle.macOS.infoPlist`? Hmm, let me check the schema file.

Let me grep the desktop-schema.json for relevant keys.

2. Whether OpenAI-compatible audio/transcriptions is a reasonable assumption for the target (Ollama? The repo's default is `http://localhost:8001/v1` with llama-cpp-python, and docs/local-llm.md says llama-cpp-python server). llama-cpp-python server DOES support `/v1/audio/transcriptions` when built with whisper support. Ollama does not have an audio transcription endpoint (it has multimodal input for chat but not whisper). Hmm.

So a "server-side STT via the configured OpenAI-compatible base_url" approach would work for llama-cpp-python but not for Ollama.

3. Whether to use the browser Web Speech API as the primary (no backend needed) and server-side as fallback.

Let me check the Tauri schema for macOS bundle config options.

Actually, let me step back and think about the brainstorming skill's requirements. The skill says: ask the user questions, one at a time, get grounding. I have a good understanding of the codebase. The key decisions that are genuinely the user's to make:

- **Scope**: browser SPA only, or also the Tauri desktop app? And also the CLI?
- **Transcription engine**: browser-native (free, no deps, Chrome-only) vs. server-side STT (works everywhere, needs a Whisper-compatible endpoint or an API key) vs. both.

# Conversational Generative UI for The Living Studio — design

**Status:** approved for implementation
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Scope:** `apps/studio` (React SPA + Tauri) and `apps/studio-api` (FastAPI sidecar)

## Intent

The Studio's agent is its product. Today that agent's intelligence is trapped in
prose: it can reason about an opportunity landscape, but it can only *describe*
the landscape. Everything it knows arrives as a wall of text in a `pre-wrap`
bubble, so the user has to read, translate, and then go click a canvas tab to
see the thing they were just told about.

The conversational experience should let the agent **hand you things**. When it
scores an outcome, you get the outcome card. When it pressure-tests a bet, you
get the before/after simulation. When it cites a customer, you get the quote with
its lineage. Prose introduces the artifact; the artifact carries the evidence.

That is the whole idea. Everything below exists to make it safe, modular, and
quiet enough to feel effortless.

## Goals

1. The agent can compose rich surfaces from a **closed, typed catalog** — no
   HTML, no eval, no arbitrary code, ever.
2. Rich surfaces render **inline in the transcript**, interleaved with prose in
   the order the agent produced them.
3. The catalog is **owned by the client** and published to the sidecar per
   request, so there is exactly one source of truth.
4. Every card can offer **actions**, which dispatch a typed intent back to the
   agent. Cards are views, never actors.
5. Degradation is graceful and total: unknown type → a quiet fallback node;
   unparseable spec → the prose still reads; no LLM → a designed demo that still
   shows real cards.

## Non-goals

- **No third-party/remote catalogs.** The catalog ships with the app. The wire
  format is compatible with a future A2UI-style multi-catalog world, but v1 does
  not accept a catalog from anywhere but the trusted client build.
- **No direct data mutation from cards.** Actions produce prompts. The agent
  keeps the single authority and the single audit trail.
- **No prose-embedded UI extraction.** Guessing at fenced blocks in model output
  reintroduces a second, unvalidated protocol path. One path only.
- **No WYSIWYG layout editor.** The agent composes; the human reacts.

## Architecture

Three layers and one contract.

# Conversational Generative UI — implementation plan

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-conversational-generative-ui-design.md`
**Goal:** The agent composes validated rich surfaces from a closed catalog, rendered
inline in the transcript, with actions that return intents to the agent.

**Tech:** React 19 + TS + Vite + vitest (no new deps); FastAPI + pydantic (no new deps);
JSON Schema (draft 2020-12 subset) as the single wire contract.

**Execution note:** no subagent tool is available in this harness, so tasks run inline
in order.

---

## Task 1 — Client protocol (`apps/studio/src/ui/protocol.ts`)

Types `UiSpec`, `UiNode`, `UiPropSchema`, `UiCatalogManifest`. Implements
`parseUiSpec(raw, manifest)` → `{ ok: true, node } | { ok: false, reason }`:

- structural checks (object, `type` string, `props` object, `children` array)
- limits: depth 12, 200 nodes, 2000-char strings, 32 children, 40 actions
- catalog lookup; unknown type → retained as `{ type, props: {} }` marked unsupported
- per-prop validation: `string | number | boolean | integer`, `enum`, `minimum`,
  `maximum`, `items`, `minItems`/`maxItems`, nested `object` fields, `required`
- unknown props stripped

Tests: valid tree accepted; unknown type tolerated; wrong prop type rejected; depth and
node ceilings enforced; children rejected on leaves; unknown props stripped; non-object
rejected.

## Task 2 — Catalog manifest (`apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts`)

`CATALOG` — 9 primitives + 6 cards, each `{ type, kind, description, acceptsChildren,
actions?, props: JSONSchema }`. `catalogManifest()` returns the serializable projection
sent to the sidecar. `catalogPrompt()` returns the human-readable block used in the
system prompt and tool description.

Tests: unique type names; every entry has a description; `catalogManifest()` is
JSON-round-trippable; every card accepts `actions`; only layout nodes accept children.

## Task 3 — Primitives (`apps/studio/src/ui/primitives.tsx`)

`Stack`, `Grid`, `Heading`, `Text`, `ListBlock`, `Stat`, `Meter`, `Callout`, `Divider`,
plus the shared `ActionRow`. All styling by class name against `theme.css`.

## Task 4 — Cards (`apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx`)

`OutcomeCard`, `OpportunityBoard`, `ImpactSimulation`, `EvidenceQuote`, `JobMap`,
`DecisionRecord`. Cards compute the ODI opportunity score from
`lib/odi.ts` when `opportunityScore` is absent — the formula has one home.

## Task 5 — Renderer (`apps/studio/src/ui/UiRenderer.tsx`, `registry.ts`)

`NODE_COMPONENTS` maps type → component. `UiRenderer` walks the tree recursively,
wraps each node in a boundary, resolves actions through `UiActionContext`.
`UnknownNode` fallback names the unknown type.

Tests: renders an outcome card with computed score; unknown type renders a fallback that
names it; clicking an action calls `onIntent` with the intent text; a throwing card does
not kill siblings; actions disabled while busy.

## Task 6 — Inline-markdown (`apps/studio/src/ui/RichText.tsx`)

Paragraphs, `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``, `[label](url)`, `- ` bullets, `###`
headings. No HTML injection path. Tests cover each construct and escaping.

## Task 7 — Chat state (`types.ts`, `StudioContext.tsx`)

`ChatPart`, `UiSpec`, extended `ChatMessage`/`ChatStreamRequest`. `sendMessage` builds
parts; `ui` SSE events append `{kind:"ui"}` parts; `message` events replace text parts;

Now I have a good understanding. Let me write the design doc and plan. But first, let me check the settings panel and how settings persist, plus what needs to be added for the transcription model field. Also need to check `defaults()` in probes.py, `llm_profile.json` handling in CLI profile.py.

Let me also verify the studio-api test layout to know where to add tests.

Let me now write the design spec. But first let me confirm a couple of remaining design details with the user, since the "Both, with fallback" answer has implications.

Actually, let me think about the architecture carefully first.

**Requirements from answers:**
1. STT: Both browser Web Speech API + sidecar OpenAI-compatible STT, with fallback.
2. Surfaces: Web SPA + Tauri desktop.
3. Interaction: Record → transcribe → review in textarea → send. Never auto-send.
4. Config: Reuse LLM base_url + api_key, new model field for transcription model.

**Design:**

### Layer 1: SPA (apps/studio)

New module: `apps/studio/src/voice/` containing:
- `types.ts` — `VoiceCapture` interface, `TranscriptionResult`
- `browserSpeech.ts` — Web Speech API adapter (SpeechRecognition). Chrome/Edge only. Produces partial + final transcripts. **Important caveat**: Web Speech API in Chrome sends audio to Google servers. Also, Tauri WKWebView does NOT implement SpeechRecognition.
- `mediaRecorder.ts` — MediaRecorder capture → Blob → upload to sidecar
- `useVoiceInput.ts` — React hook orchestrating: pick engine, record, transcribe, report status
- `MicButton.tsx` — the UI component

Hmm, wait. The "Both, with fallback" — which is primary? Let me think about what's actually best.

Browser Web Speech API:
- Pros: no backend needed, live streaming, free
- Cons: Chrome/Edge only, audio goes to Google, not available in Firefox/Safari/Tauri WKWebView, non-standard API (webkitSpeechRecognition), no confidence scores, no audio file retained

Sidecar STT:
- Pros: works everywhere the SPA runs (including Tauri), consistent with "SPA never talks to backend directly", works with local whisper servers, audio file can be retained/inspected
- Cons: needs an STT endpoint, not live, needs ffmpeg for some formats? Actually no — the OpenAI transcriptions API accepts webm/opus? Let me think. OpenAI's Whisper API accepts: flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, webm. So webm/opus from MediaRecorder is accepted by OpenAI. Local servers (whisper.cpp server, faster-whisper-server) accept similar. So no ffmpeg needed for the common case.

The most important architectural point: the sidecar path works in Tauri; the browser path doesn't. So sidecar should be the **primary**, browser SpeechRecognition as the fallback when the sidecar STT fails/unavailable? Or the other way around?

Actually re-reading the user's answer: "Both, with fallback". The description I gave was: "Browser Speech API when present, sidecar STT as fallback. More code, two code paths, but works everywhere."

So: browser SpeechRecognition when present, sidecar STT as fallback. That's what the user selected. But the label ordering suggested browser-first. Let me be careful — I labeled the option "Both, with fallback" with description "Browser Speech API when present, sidecar STT as fallback." The user picked that. So browser-first.

Hmm, but that has a real downside for Tauri: Tauri WKWebView doesn't have SpeechRecognition, so Tauri always uses sidecar. And in the browser, Chrome's SpeechRecognition sends audio to Google. Given the project is a local-first, privacy-conscious ODI tool where the whole point is "the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM directly" — sending mic audio to Google silently would be a meaningful architectural violation.

This is a genuine tension worth flagging. But I offered the option with that description and the user chose it. Let me think about how to reconcile.

Actually — a good resolution: make the engine **user-selectable and explicit**, defaulting to the sidecar (private/local), with the browser API offered as an alternative. But that adds settings UI complexity.

Hmm, but actually let me reconsider. The cleanest reading that honors both "Both, with fallback" AND the project's architectural invariant:

- **Sidecar is the default engine** (preserves "SPA never talks to a model provider directly", works in Tauri, works with local whisper, keeps audio local).
- **Browser SpeechRecognition is the fallback** when the sidecar STT is unavailable/unconfigured (e.g., user has no whisper endpoint running, or STT call fails).

This is "Both, with fallback" — just with the fallback ordering that matches the architecture. And critically, it means the *default* path never leaks audio to a third party.

But the user might specifically want live streaming in the browser. Hmm.

Actually, let me reconsider once more. There's a subtlety: the browser SpeechRecognition API is the ONLY way to get a *live* transcript. The sidecar path is inherently record-then-transcribe. The user chose "Record, transcribe, review, send" as the interaction, not "Live streaming transcript into the input". So the live-streaming benefit of the browser API is not what's being asked for.

Given the interaction model chosen (record → transcribe → review → send), the browser SpeechRecognition path actually fits well too: it can use `continuous = false` and `interimResults = false`, and on result it just yields the final transcript. That's a record-then-transcribe shape.

OK. I'll make a decision and state it clearly, flagging it as my call: **sidecar first, browser fallback**, with the browser path explicitly opt-out-able. Actually — let me make it simplest and most honest:

Decision: **Sidecar STT is the default and primary path. Browser SpeechRecognition is the fallback when the sidecar has no working STT endpoint.** The user can also explicitly pick an engine in Settings. Actually, let me keep it simpler: no engine picker in settings; just the fallback chain. Hmm, but "Both, with fallback" and a user might want to force the browser one.

Let me add a small settings toggle: "Voice engine: Auto (server) / Browser / Server only". Actually that's over-engineering for v1. Let me do:
- Settings field: `transcription_model` (new field, per the config answer) and `transcription_base_url` optional? No — user said reuse base_url + api_key, new model field.

Hmm wait. There's a problem with reusing base_url for STT: the LLM base_url is `http://localhost:8001/v1` (llama-cpp). llama-cpp-python's server does NOT serve `/audio/transcriptions`. So reusing base_url means STT will fail against the default local LLM. The user explicitly chose "Reuse LLM base_url + api_key, new model field" over "Separate transcription config block" though.

I should honor the choice but make it work: the sidecar calls `POST {base_url}/audio/transcriptions` with `model={transcription_model}`. If the user's LLM server doesn't serve it, they point the LLM base_url at a server that does (e.g. OpenAI, or a LocalAI/whisper server) or they rely on the browser fallback. But that conflates chat and STT servers...

Better approach that honors the choice and is actually sane: add an **optional** `transcription_base_url` that defaults to empty → falls back to `base_url`. That's a superset of the chosen option: "reuse base_url + api_key" is still the default behavior, and there's an escape hatch. But the user chose NOT to have a separate config block...

Hmm. Let me re-read: "Reuse LLM base_url + api_key, new model field. Fewest moving parts, but requires your LLM server to also serve /audio/transcriptions." The user accepted that tradeoff knowingly. OK — I'll honor it exactly: reuse base_url + api_key, add `transcription_model` field. No separate base_url. If it fails, the browser fallback kicks in, and the error message will say "your base_url does not serve /audio/transcriptions".

That's clean, honest, and matches the chosen tradeoff. Good.

### Now the detailed architecture.

**Sidecar (`apps/studio-api`):**

New file: `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/transcribe.py`
- `async def transcribe(request: TranscriptionRequest) -> dict` — accepts an uploaded audio file + base_url + api_key + model, calls OpenAI-compatible `POST {base_url}/audio/transcriptions` with multipart.
- Reuses `AsyncOpenAI(base_url=..., api_key=...).audio.transcriptions.create(file=..., model=...)`.

New endpoint in `router.py`:
```python
@router.post("/transcribe")
async def post_transcribe(
    file: UploadFile = File(...),
    base_url: str = Form(...),
    api_key: str = Form(""),
    model: str = Form(...),
) -> dict:
    return await transcribe_audio(...)
```

Requires `python-multipart` — already installed transitively via fastmcp/starlette, but must be added as an explicit dependency of `apps/studio-api` (FastAPI raises a RuntimeError at request time if it's missing, but it's not in the direct deps). Add `python-multipart>=0.0.18` to `apps/studio-api/pyproject.toml`.

New schema in `schemas.py`:
```python
class TranscribeResponse(BaseModel):
    text: str
    language: str | None = None
    duration: float | None = None
```

Also `probes.py` `defaults()` should get a `transcription_model` default, e.g. `"whisper-1"` and env `AGENTIC_ODI_TRANSCRIBE_MODEL`.

Also `StudioConfig` in the SPA types gains `transcription_model: string`.

Wait — but `defaults()` in probes.py returns the StudioConfig defaults which the SPA reads from `/api/config`. Adding `transcription_model` there keeps it consistent. And `llm_profile.json` in the CLI (apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/profile.py) — should I add it there? The CLI is out of scope for the mic. But the profile is shared (probes.py `_load_profile_fallback` reads llm_profile.json). Let me check whether adding a key to `defaults()` breaks the CLI profile. `defaults()` just reads keys from the profile dict if present — adding a new key is safe. But `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/profile.py` may have a fixed schema. Let me check.

**SPA (`apps/studio`):**

New directory `apps/studio/src/voice/`:
- `speechRecognition.ts` — typed wrapper around `window.SpeechRecognition | window.webkitSpeechRecognition`. Feature-detect. Exposes `isBrowserSpeechSupported()`.
- `recorder.ts` — `MediaRecorder` capture. Feature-detect `navigator.mediaDevices?.getUserMedia` and `window.MediaRecorder`. Handles mimeType selection (webm/opus preferred, mp4 fallback for Safari), start/stop, returns Blob + mimeType.
- `useVoiceInput.ts` — the orchestrator hook: state machine `idle | recording | transcribing | error`, `start()`, `stop()`, `transcribe(blob)`.
- `MicButton.tsx` — renders the button with states, aria labels.

Wiring into `ChatCopilot.tsx`:
- Mic button next to the textarea inside `.chat-input-row`.
- On transcript result → set draft (append to existing draft), focus textarea, user reviews and hits Send.
- Never auto-send.

API client: `apps/studio/src/api/studioApi.ts` → add `transcribeAudio({blob, baseUrl, apiKey, model})` posting FormData to `/api/transcribe`.

**Fallback chain in `useVoiceInput`:**
1. If `MediaRecorder` + `getUserMedia` available → record. On stop:
   a. Try sidecar transcribe. If success → done.
   b. If sidecar transcribe fails (network error, 404, non-2xx) AND browser SpeechRecognition is supported → fall back to browser speech recognition.
   
   Hmm, but that's weird ordering: you already recorded, then you run speech recognition on the *live* mic, requiring the user to speak again. That's a bad UX.

Better fallback ordering: decide the **engine before recording**.
- If the sidecar STT is known-reachable (we can probe it) → record with MediaRecorder → transcribe on server.
- Else if browser SpeechRecognition is available → use it (it captures live).
- Else → error: mic unsupported.

But probing the STT endpoint requires a request. We could probe it lazily: try server STT once; if it fails, remember "server STT unavailable" and switch to browser engine for subsequent attempts. And for the *current* attempt, if the server fails and the browser engine is available, we can prompt the user "Server transcription unavailable — retry with the browser engine?" That's a bit clunky.

Cleaner: **The engine is chosen per attempt, with a preference, and the fallback is a retry the user can trigger.** Hmm.

Alternative much cleaner design: **Run the browser engine and the server engine at the same time? No.**

Let me think about what actually happens in practice:
- Browser (Chrome/Edge) + server STT working: use server. 
- Browser (Chrome/Edge) + no server STT: use browser speech.
- Tauri: no browser speech → server only.

The cleanest is: **remember the last known working engine** in localStorage, default to server. On a server-transcribe failure, automatically retry with the browser engine *in the same recording session* — but the browser engine needs live audio...

OK here's the thing — the browser SpeechRecognition API can be started *before* recording begins and both can run concurrently. I.e., we could start BOTH the MediaRecorder and the SpeechRecognition at the same time. Then:
- Server path: uses the MediaRecorder blob → server transcription.
- Browser path: uses the SpeechRecognition final transcript.
- Whichever succeeds first wins; the other is discarded.

That's actually elegant and gives a true "both with fallback" with a single user action. Downside: Chrome's SpeechRecognition sends audio to Google even if the server path wins. Privacy concern.

Hmm. But wait — I already decided sidecar-first is the default for privacy. Let me reconsider whether to just ask the user.

Actually — let me step back and not over-engineer. Let me re-read the user's selection: "Both, with fallback". The option description said: "Browser Speech API when present, sidecar STT as fallback. More code, two code paths, but works everywhere."

So the user accepted: browser-first, sidecar as fallback. I should implement that, since the user chose it explicitly. But I flagged in the option description that it sends audio to Google, and the user still chose it. And they said "works everywhere" — which means the sidecar fallback is what makes Tauri work.

So: **Browser SpeechRecognition when present (live, one-shot); sidecar STT as fallback.**

But then how does the sidecar fallback work in Chrome if the browser engine is present? It wouldn't — the browser engine is present in Chrome, so Chrome always uses the browser engine, and Tauri (no browser engine) always uses the sidecar. The "fallback" then means: if the browser engine *errors out* (permission denied, network error, unsupported language), fall back to the sidecar. But in Chrome, if the browser engine fails at the *start* (getUserMedia permission denied), the sidecar path would also fail (it needs the mic too). If the browser engine fails *mid-session* (network error to Google), the sidecar can't recover the already-spoken audio.

Hmm, so a meaningful fallback requires both running concurrently, OR choosing the engine up-front.

**Decision: run them concurrently but in a controlled way.**

Actually, let me reconsider one more time, and go with the design that is simplest to reason about and test, and that the user's chosen description supports:

**Engine selection up-front, with a persisted preference and a runtime fallback:**

1. `voiceEngine` setting: `"auto" | "browser" | "server"`. Default `"auto"`.
2. `"auto"` resolves at capture time:
   - If `SpeechRecognition` is available AND the server STT is not known-good → browser.
   - Else → server.
3. On a failure, we surface a clear error with a **Retry using the other engine** affordance (a toast action or just a message). This is honest: we don't silently re-record.

Hmm, "auto" needs to know if server STT is good. We can probe: the sidecar can expose `POST /api/health/stt` that does a cheap reachability check on the STT endpoint (like `is_endpoint_reachable` for the socket, plus optionally a `GET /models` check on the base_url to see if a transcription model is listed). Actually a good probe: `GET {base_url}/models` and check if `transcription_model` is in the list. That's exactly what `check_llm_health` does (lists models). For a llama-cpp server the model list won't include `whisper-1` → probe says "not available" → browser engine chosen. For OpenAI, `whisper-1` is listed → server engine chosen. For LocalAI/whisper.cpp server, models list may or may not include it.

That's a solid, testable probe! And it directly solves the "your LLM server doesn't serve /audio/transcriptions" problem: we detect it up front and pick the browser engine automatically, with a clear toast explaining why.

So:
- `POST /api/health/stt` with `{base_url, api_key, model}` → `{available: bool, message: str}`. Implementation: reachability + `models.list()` + check whether the transcription model is present. If models.list() fails or model absent → unavailable, with a message naming the model.
- The SPA calls it (debounced / on settings change) and caches the result.
- `voiceEngine` = "auto" → server if probe says available, else browser if supported, else error toast explaining.

Then the "fallback" is real and automatic: on Chrome with a local llama-cpp LLM (the project's documented default setup!), the probe fails → browser engine. On Tauri → no browser engine → server engine, and if the probe fails we tell the user exactly what to configure.

Wait, but hold on: on Tauri, if the probe fails, we have NO engine. So we need a clear error: "Your LLM backend does not serve /audio/transcriptions (model 'whisper-1'). Point base_url at a transcription-capable server, or use the browser." Good — that's a real, actionable error.

Hmm, but the browser engine in Tauri: WKWebView on macOS — does it support SpeechRecognition? Safari does not support the Web Speech API's SpeechRecognition (Safari 14.1+ supports it partially actually — Safari does support `webkitSpeechRecognition` on macOS/iOS). WKWebView might. Uncertain. We'll feature-detect at runtime, so it degrades gracefully.

OK, this is a solid design. Let me also handle: what if the user is in a browser without SpeechRecognition (Firefox)? Then server engine is required. Fine.

**Also: browser engine vs "record → transcribe → review" interaction.** With SpeechRecognition, the user clicks mic → speaks → clicks stop (or the API auto-finalizes on silence) → final transcript appears in the textarea → user reviews → sends. This matches the chosen interaction. 

For the server engine: click mic → speak → click stop → blob uploaded → transcription → text appears in textarea → review → send. Also matches.

**MediaRecorder mimeType**: prefer `audio/webm;codecs=opus`, fallback `audio/webm`, `audio/mp4` (Safari), `audio/ogg;codecs=opus`.

Note: Safari (webkit) supports MediaRecorder with audio/mp4 since Safari 14.1. OpenAI's transcriptions API accepts mp4/m4a. Good.

**Max duration**: cap recording at e.g. 120s to avoid huge uploads. Actually, let's cap at 60s? OpenAI limit is 25MB. Let me set a 120s cap and a size guard.

**Now, the Tauri desktop part:**

Per the GitHub issues:
- macOS: needs `Info.plist` with `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` AND a separate entitlements plist with `com.apple.security.device.microphone` + `com.apple.security.device.audio-input`. Configured via `bundle.macOS.infoPlist` and `bundle.macOS.entitlements` in tauri.conf.json.
- Linux/WebKitGTK: `getUserMedia` may fail with NotAllowedError even with a permission-request hook (issue #15277, closed as "completed" — let me check the resolution). The fix typically requires the `webkit2gtk` `media` feature? Hmm. Actually there's a known workaround: set `app.security.csp` ... no. For WebKitGTK, Tauri v2 has a `with_webview` hook to `connect_permission_request`. Issue #15277 was closed as completed on 2026-04-21 — let me check what the resolution was. Let me look at the comments.

Let me fetch the issue comments for #15277 to see the resolution.

Also, for the Tauri app, the dev URL is `http://localhost:5173` — **`getUserMedia` requires a secure context** (HTTPS or localhost). `http://localhost:5173` IS a secure context (localhost is treated as potentially trustworthy). And in the Tauri production build, the webview loads from `tauri://localhost` (macOS) / `http://tauri.localhost` (Windows) / `app://localhost` (Linux) — those are custom schemes. Tauri registers them as secure contexts. Let me verify: Tauri's `custom_protocol` — in wry, the Tauri protocol is served over `http://tauri.localhost` on Windows and `tauri://localhost` on macOS. Tauri v2 sets `isSecureContext` appropriately? I recall Tauri v2 does make the custom protocol a secure context (there's `Wry`'s `with_webview`...). Let me search the wry source for "secure".

Earlier grep for "isSecureContext" in wry and tauri returned nothing. Hmm. But WKWebView treats custom schemes... Actually in Tauri v2 on macOS, the URL is `tauri://localhost`, and `navigator.mediaDevices` requires a secure context. WKWebView's `isSecureContext` for `tauri://localhost` — Tauri sets `WKWebView` with `isSecureContext` true? 

Let me just check the wry source for how it handles the custom protocol and whether there's a secure context flag. Let me grep more broadly.

Let me do that research, then write the plan.

Also: I should double check that `navigator.mediaDevices` is even exposed. In WKWebView, `mediaDevices` requires the app to have the microphone entitlement AND the page to be a secure context.

Let me look at the wry crate for "secure".

Let me also check the resolution of Tauri issue #15277 for the Linux/WebKitGTK mic.

Let me do these two things in parallel.
Let me research the Tauri desktop mic constraints more precisely, since that's the riskiest part.

## Architecture

### Flow
```
User clicks mic in ChatCopilot
  → MediaRecorder via getUserMedia (browser) or Tauri webview
  → on stop: Blob (audio/webm or audio/mp4)
  → POST /api/transcribe (multipart/form-data) to sidecar
  → sidecar: openai AsyncOpenAI(base_url=settings.base_url).audio.transcriptions.create(model=..., file=...)
  → returns {text}

  → user reviews, presses Send → existing sendMessage(text) path
```

### Two STT paths (user chose "Both, with fallback")
1. **Browser Web Speech API** (`window.SpeechRecognition` / `webkitSpeechRecognition`) — used when available. Gives live interim results directly as text, no backend round trip. Chrome/Edge only.
2. **Sidecar STT** (OpenAI-compatible `/audio/transcriptions`) — fallback. Record with MediaRecorder, POST blob.

- If `SpeechRecognition` is available: start recognition, show interim transcript live in the textarea (as a ghost/interim), on final result → commit to draft.
- Else: start MediaRecorder, on stop → upload → sidecar transcribes → commit to draft.

Both paths end at the same place: "text lands in the draft for review, user presses Send."

# Voice Chat — speaking to the copilot — design

**Status:** approved for implementation
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Scope:** `apps/studio` (React SPA + Tauri 2 shell) and `apps/studio-api` (FastAPI sidecar)

## Intent

The Living Studio's copilot already accepts a typed prompt and answers with
evidence. The friction is the keyboard. A PM describing a customer struggle is
often mid-thought, mid-call, or hands-busy; typing the sentence costs more than
saying it. The studio should let a person **speak** to the copilot and get the
same agent behaviour they get from typing.

The non-negotiable property: **speech enters through the same door as text.**
A spoken message becomes a plain user string in the chat transcript, reviewed
in the same textarea, and sent by the same `sendMessage` call. Nothing about
the agent, the MCP tools, the tool-loop, or the ODI domain changes. Voice is an
input device, not a feature of the agent.

Today the repository contains **zero** audio capability — no mic, no recording,
no speech-to-text, in the working tree, in any of the 30+ `.worktrees/`
checkouts, or anywhere in git history. This is built from scratch.

## Goals

1. The user can record speech from the chat input and get the transcript
   placed in the textarea for review, then send it like any other message.
2. Audio never reaches the LLM as audio. Transcription happens in the
   sidecar, against the OpenAI-compatible backend the studio already talks to.
3. The mic works in the browser SPA **and** in the Tauri desktop shell, or it
   fails with a message that says exactly why.
4. The whole feature degrades to "type your message" if any part of it is
   unavailable — no dead buttons, no half-states.
5. Zero new runtime dependencies on the Python side beyond what the workspace
   already resolves (`python-multipart` is already in the lockfile via
   `fastmcp`/`starlette`; it is promoted to a direct dependency of the
   sidecar so the intent is explicit).

## Non-goals

- **No speech-to-text of the agent's reply.** The copilot stays text-only on
  the way out. TTS is a separate decision with its own latency and voice
  selection problems.
- **No streaming/partial transcripts.** The user asked for
  *record → transcribe → review → send*. A live partial transcript needs a
  streaming STT endpoint, is noisier, and buys little for a 5–30 second PM
  utterance.
- **No push-to-talk, no auto-send.** Nothing is sent to the agent without an
  explicit Send press. This matches the existing rule that cards are views,
  never actors: the human keeps the single authority and the single audit
  trail. A mis-transcribed auto-send would create ODI records nobody meant to
  create.
- **No mic in the CLI REPL** (`apps/cli`). The CLI's entry point is
  `input("you › ")`; giving it a mic means a Python audio-capture dependency
  and a second transcription path for a surface that is explicitly the
  terminal fallback.
- **No vendored or bundled speech model.** Transcription is delegated to
  whatever OpenAI-compatible `/audio/transcriptions` endpoint the user points
  the studio at. The studio does not download weights.

## Architecture

Four pieces and one rule: **the SPA never talks to the model directly.** Voice
follows the same boundary that `base_url` / `api_key` / `model` already obey.

```text
┌──────────────────────── apps/studio (React 19 + TS) ─────────────────────────┐
│                                                                              │
│  components/chat/MicButton.tsx          lib/recorder.ts                     │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────┐      ┌──────────────────────────────┐      │
│  │ idle │ recording │ transcribing│      │ getUserMedia + MediaRecorder│      │
│  │ disabled when unsupported     │─────▶│ → Blob (audio/webm)          │      │
│  └──────────────────────────────┘      │ → SpeechRecognition (if any) │      │
│         │                             └──────────────────────────────┘      │
│         │ transcript lands in the textarea draft                            │
│         ▼                                                                    │
│  ChatCopilot.tsx  <textarea onChange → setDraft>  (unchanged contract)       │
│                                                                              │
│  api/studioApi.ts                                                          │
│    transcribeAudio(blob) ──POST /api/transcribe (multipart)──┐              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────┘
                                                               │
                          ┌────────────────────────────────────▼─────────────┐
                          │ apps/studio-api (FastAPI sidecar)                │
                          │  studio/router.py   POST /api/transcribe        │
                          │  studio/transcribe.py                            │
                          │    ├─ path A: browser SpeechRecognition           │
                          │    │    (client-side, no request at all)         │
                          │    └─ path B: POST audio → OpenAI-compatible     │
                          │         /audio/transcriptions (whisper-1, …)     │
                          └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### The two transcription paths

The user chose **"both, with fallback"**. The SPA tries the cheapest path
first and falls back to the second when it is unavailable.

**Path A — browser `SpeechRecognition` (no network round-trip).**
`window.SpeechRecognition` / `webkitSpeechRecognition` is present in Chrome,
Edge, and Safari 14.1+. It streams interim results and yields a final
transcript with no upload to us. It is **not** present in Firefox, and it is
**not** reliably present in the Tauri WKWebView on Linux.

**Path B — sidecar transcription (works everywhere the mic works).**
The SPA records audio with `getUserMedia` + `MediaRecorder`, POSTs the blob as
`multipart/form-data` to `/api/transcribe`, and the sidecar forwards it to
`{base_url}/audio/transcriptions` using the studio's existing `api_key`. The
sidecar returns `{"text": "..."}`.

The SPA picks Path A when `SpeechRecognition` exists **and** the user is in a
browser context; otherwise it uses Path B. If Path A fails at runtime, the
button offers Path B explicitly rather than silently dying. The user can always
override the choice in Settings.

Why the sidecar owns Path B rather than the SPA calling the model endpoint
directly: the studio's existing rule is that the SPA never holds the model
credential path for anything but what the sidecar already proxies
(`/api/chat`, `/api/health/llm`). Audio is a bigger secret and a bigger
payload than a prompt; it should not be a new egress path from the browser.

## Data flow

### Recording (Path B)

1. User clicks the mic button. The button enters `recording` state.
2. `lib/recorder.ts` calls `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: true })`.
   - Rejection (permission denied, no device, insecure context) → toast with a
     specific reason, button returns to `idle`.
3. `MediaRecorder` starts with a MIME type chosen from a capability probe
   (`audio/webm;codecs=opus` first, then `audio/webm`, then `audio/mp4`, then
   browser default). Safari only offers `audio/mp4`; Whisper accepts both.
4. Chunks accumulate. A live elapsed-time indicator shows in the button.
5. User clicks again (or presses `Escape`). Recording stops, the stream's
   tracks are stopped, and the `Blob` is assembled.
6. The blob is POSTed to `/api/transcribe`.

### Sidecar transcription

`POST /api/transcribe`

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `audio` | file (multipart) | The recorded blob. |
| `base_url` | str | Reuses the studio's LLM base URL. |
| `api_key` | str | Reuses the studio's LLM API key. |
| `model` | str | Transcription model, e.g. `whisper-1`. |
| `language` | str | Optional ISO code; omitted means "auto-detect". |

Response `200`: `{"text": "<transcript>", "model": "<model>"}`

Failures:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `400` | No audio, or the audio was empty. |
| `415` | Unsupported audio type. |
| `502` | The transcription backend refused or was unreachable. The upstream message is passed through in `detail` so the user can see what the backend said. |
| `413` | Audio exceeds the size cap (see below). |

The sidecar uses `openai.AsyncOpenAI(base_url=...).audio.transcriptions.create(...)`
with the file tuple `("<name>", bytes, "<mime>")` and `response_format="text"`.
It passes the upstream error text through rather than swallowing it — a
misconfigured `base_url` is the most likely failure and the user needs the
backend's own words to fix it.

**Size cap:** 20 MB per request, enforced by the sidecar before the upload is
forwarded. A 20 MB cap is roughly 30+ minutes of opus audio; a PM utterance is
seconds. The cap exists to stop a runaway recording from becoming an
unbounded upload.

### Back in the SPA

The transcript is appended to the textarea draft (not to the transcript), the
textarea is focused, and the caret is placed at the end. The user reads it,
fixes it if the recognizer mangled a product term, and presses Send — the
existing `submit` path, unchanged.

If the transcript is empty, the draft is untouched and a toast says the
recording produced no speech.

## Configuration

Reuse the studio's existing `base_url` and `api_key`. **One new field:**

| Setting | Env var | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `transcription_model` | `AGENTIC_ODI_TRANSCRIBE_MODEL` | `whisper-1` | Model name sent to `/audio/transcriptions`. |

The transcription endpoint is derived: `{base_url}/audio/transcriptions`. This
is the OpenAI-compatible convention, and it means any backend that serves
chat completions at `base_url` and Whisper at the standard path works with no
extra configuration — `llama-cpp-python`, LocalAI, faster-whisper-server,
Ollama, vLLM, or OpenAI itself.

The sidecar's `defaults()` (in `studio/probes.py`) gains the new key so
`GET /api/config` returns it and the SPA's settings panel can prefill it.
`StudioConfig` in `apps/studio/src/types.ts` gains the matching field, and
`EMPTY_CONFIG` gains the default. The setting is persisted in the same
`localStorage["studio.settings"]` blob as the rest, so it survives restarts
without a new storage key.

**Requirement this creates:** the backend must serve `/audio/transcriptions`.
A backend that serves only chat completions will fail transcription with a
clear `502` naming the missing route. The Settings panel and the docs both
state this requirement, and the mic button is disabled with an explanatory
tooltip when the transcription model is blank.

## Desktop (Tauri) specifics

The Tauri shell currently declares only `core:default` and `updater:default`
in `apps/studio/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json`. Microphone access needs
three things.

**1. A permission handler.** Tauri 2 exposes
`Builder::on_permission_request(|webview, kind| ...)`, and
`PermissionKind::Microphone` is a first-class variant. The handler returns
`PermissionResponse::Allow` for `Microphone` and `Default` for everything
else, so the webview's own behaviour is preserved for other permission kinds.
Tauri documents this path as "Fully supported" on macOS (via
`WKUIDelegate::requestMediaCapturePermission`), Linux (via WebKitGTK's
`permission-request` signal), and Windows (via WebView2's
`PermissionRequested` event).

**2. macOS bundle metadata.** A `Info.plist` with `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`
so macOS can ask the user, and — for the notarized/sandboxed build — a
separate entitlements file carrying `com.apple.security.device.microphone` and
`com.apple.security.device.audio-input`. Both are referenced from
`tauri.conf.json` under `bundle.macOS.infoPlist` and `bundle.macOS.entitlements`.

The entitlements file must be **separate** from the `Info.plist`. Tauri issue
#8314 documents that putting the `com.apple.security.device.*` keys in the
`Info.plist` merges them into the bundle's plist where they have no effect,
and that moving them to a dedicated entitlements file is what made
`getUserMedia` work in a signed build. `bundle.macOS.entitlements` expects a
path relative to the `tauri.conf.json` directory.

**3. Linux.** The WebKitGTK `permission-request` signal fires the handler, but
the underlying PulseAudio/PipeWire capture still needs the OS-level
permission. On Wayland this is the desktop portal. Tauri issue #15277 records
a case where the Rust-side `allow()` was not sufficient on Wayland; the
reported cause was the caller's own integration path rather than an upstream
Tauri defect, and the issue was closed. The design therefore does not
promise a one-click Linux desktop experience, and the docs say so plainly.

**Known asymmetry between dev and release.** On macOS, `getUserMedia` behaves
differently in `tauri dev` versus a packaged `.app`: `Info.plist` is only
honoured inside a real bundle, and in dev the *terminal* process inherits the
microphone TCC permission instead of the app. Tauri issue #10878 documents
this. The desktop mic must be verified against a **packaged build**
(`npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri build`), not only `tauri dev`.

## Interaction states

The mic button is a single control that changes appearance and label:

| State | Appearance | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `idle` | Mic icon, "Record" label | Ready. |
| `recording` | Pulsing red dot, elapsed time, "Stop" label | Capturing. |
| `transcribing` | Spinner, "Transcribing…" label | Audio uploaded, awaiting text. |
| `unsupported` | Mic icon, disabled, tooltip explains | No mic, or no secure context, or no transcription model configured. |

Keyboard: `Escape` while recording stops it and discards the audio.

Accessibility: the button carries `aria-label` that changes with state
("Record voice message" / "Stop recording" / "Transcribing voice message"),
and `aria-live="polite"` on the elapsed-time region so a screen reader
announces the recording state without spamming.

Disabled while a reply is streaming (`streaming === true`) — the studio is
one conversation, and a half-finished reply should not be interrupted by a
recording.

## Failure handling

Every failure mode has one specific message, because a mic that fails
vaguely is a mic nobody trusts.

| Condition | Message |
|---|---|
| `navigator.mediaDevices` missing | "This browser cannot record audio. Use the desktop app or a Chromium browser." |
| Insecure context (not `https:` or `localhost`) | "Recording needs a secure connection. Open the studio over https or on localhost." |
| Permission denied | "Microphone access was denied. Allow it in your browser's site settings." |
| No audio device | "No microphone was found." |
| `MediaRecorder` unsupported | "This browser cannot record audio." |
| Backend has no `/audio/transcriptions` | "The configured model backend has no transcription endpoint (/audio/transcriptions)." |
| Backend unreachable | "Could not reach the transcription backend." |
| Empty transcript | "No speech was detected in that recording." |

Errors surface as a toast (`pushToast("error", …)` in `StudioContext`), which
is the studio's existing error channel, and the button returns to `idle`.

## What does not change

- `StudioContext.sendMessage` — untouched. Voice produces a string; the string
  path is the text path.
- The SSE chat protocol, the tool loop, the MCP client, the ODI domain, the
  `render_ui` catalog — untouched.
- The CLI — untouched.
- The MCP server — untouched. Voice is not a tool; it is an input device.

## Testing strategy

**Sidecar (`apps/studio-api/tests/`)**

- `/api/transcribe` returns the upstream text for a small fake audio upload.
- A missing `audio` part returns `400`.
- An oversized upload returns `413` without contacting the backend.
- An upstream failure returns `502` with the upstream message in `detail`.
- `defaults()` exposes the transcription model and honours
  `AGENTIC_ODI_TRANSCRIBE_MODEL`.
- The transcription call is made against `{base_url}/audio/transcriptions`
  with the studio's `api_key` — asserted on the fake client, not by hitting a
  network.

**SPA (`apps/studio/src/`)**

- `lib/recorder.ts`: mime-type selection falls back correctly; a failed
  `getUserMedia` rejects with a typed reason; the blob is assembled from
  chunks; tracks are stopped on stop.
- `MicButton`: renders the right label per state; click starts and stops;
  `Escape` stops; the button is disabled while `streaming`; the transcript is
  written into the draft and the textarea is focused.
- Path selection: `SpeechRecognition` present → Path A; absent → Path B; Path A
  runtime failure → the user is offered Path B.
- `studioApi.transcribeAudio` posts multipart and returns the text.

jsdom implements neither `MediaRecorder` nor `getUserMedia`, so both are
stubbed in the tests, following the existing pattern in
`apps/studio/src/test/setup.ts` (which already polyfills `scrollTo` and
`localStorage` for the same reason).

**Desktop**

- `tauri.conf.json` references an `Info.plist` containing
  `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` and an entitlements file containing the
  microphone keys. Asserted by a test that parses the JSON/plist files, so a
  typo in the bundle metadata fails in CI rather than at a user's first mic
  click.
- The Rust permission handler returns `Allow` for `Microphone` and `Default`
  otherwise. Asserted by a Rust unit test.

**Manual verification** (cannot be automated): grant the mic in a browser, in a
packaged Tauri build on macOS, and confirm the transcript lands in the
textarea.

## Documentation

- `README.md` — Code Overview gains the voice capability; Prerequisites
  unchanged (no new install step).
- `docs/living-studio.md` — a "Speaking to the copilot" section: the two
  paths, the `whisper-1` requirement, the settings field, and the per-platform
  desktop caveats (macOS needs a packaged build; Linux needs portal
  permission).
- `docs/local-llm.md` — the backend requirement: serving chat completions is
  no longer sufficient; `/audio/transcriptions` must exist too.
- `docs/roadmap.md` — a completed item for voice input.
- `docs/development.md` — the new test files in the coverage map.

## Open questions for the builder

None that block implementation. The following were decided by the human
partner and are recorded here as their decisions, not the agent's:

- Transcription runs in the sidecar against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint,
  with the browser `SpeechRecognition` API tried first.
- The mic ships in both the browser SPA and the Tauri desktop app.
- The interaction is record → transcribe → review → send; nothing auto-sends.
- Configuration reuses the LLM `base_url` and `api_key`, with one new model
  field.

CI only checks `git diff --exit-code -- src/api/schema.d.ts` after running `npm run gen:api-types`, which regenerates from `apps/studio/openapi.json` (a checked-in file). So `openapi.json` is a hand-maintained/stale artifact. If I add a `/api/transcribe` endpoint, I should add it to `apps/studio/openapi.json` and regenerate `src/api/schema.d.ts`, otherwise CI's drift check still passes (since openapi.json itself is the source), but the types would be stale. Since the API client doesn't strictly need the generated types (studioApi.ts hand-writes types), I could skip. But best practice: update openapi.json + regenerate schema.d.ts to keep the contract honest. Let me check if openapi.json is actually in sync with the current app — it says title "Agentic ODI Local Server" but the app says "Agentic ODI Studio API". So it's already stale. I'll note it as an optional task.

Now let me check the studio-api tests folder and how the app exposes routes, plus check the `studio/` (old) dir doesn't exist. And check `scripts/dev.py`.

Let me also verify the packaging spec to see if a new dep needs PyInstaller handling.

Also, one more important check: the Cloudflare Worker proxies `/api/*` to the sidecar. A multipart POST through the worker — `request.body` is passed through with `duplex` potentially needed. Let me check: the worker does `new Request(target, {method, headers, body: request.body, redirect: "manual"})`. For a streaming body in Workers, you need `duplex: 'half'` in some runtimes. Cloudflare Workers support streaming request bodies without duplex. The headers include content-type with boundary, and the body is passed. The Content-Length header would be present in the original request and forwarded — for a streamed body that's fine since it's the same content. Actually there's a subtlety: `request.body` in Workers is a ReadableStream, and forwarding it requires the target to accept a streaming body. Cloudflare's fetch accepts it. But the `content-length` header forwarded matches the original body. OK.

But there's a real risk: the multipart upload through the Cloudflare tunnel. Cloudflare's free plan has a 100MB upload limit, so 20MB is fine.

import asyncio
import json
import logging
from typing import Any

from agentic_odi_core import ODIService, ToolName
from fastapi import HTTPException
from fastmcp import Client as McpClient

from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.probes import is_endpoint_reachable
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.seed import seed_payload

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT = 3.0


async def fetch_canvas(mcp_url: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Fetch live canvas data from FastMCP, falling back to the seed prototype."""
    jobs: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    outcomes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    warnings: list[str] = []

    if not is_endpoint_reachable(mcp_url, timeout=0.3):
        log.warning("MCP endpoint unreachable at %s — falling back to seed data", mcp_url)
        return {**seed_payload(), "source": "seed", "warnings": ["MCP endpoint unreachable"]}

    try:
        mcp_client = McpClient(mcp_url)
        async with mcp_client:
            raw_jobs = await asyncio.wait_for(
                mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_JOBS.value, {}), timeout=1.5
            )
            try:
                parsed_jobs = json.loads(str(raw_jobs))
                if isinstance(parsed_jobs, list):
                    jobs = parsed_jobs
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                log.warning("Failed to parse jobs from MCP: %s", exc)
                jobs = []

            for job in jobs:
                job_id = job.get("id")
                if not job_id:
                    continue

                try:
                    raw_steps = await asyncio.wait_for(
                        mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_JOB_MAP.value, {"job_id": job_id}),
                        timeout=1.0,
                    )
                    parsed_steps = json.loads(str(raw_steps))
                    if isinstance(parsed_steps, list):
                        steps.extend(parsed_steps)
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
